name: Guitar
description: Clean electric guitar: plucked steel strings heard through a pickup whose colour changes with every fret, a clean amplifier and a speaker, with strummed chords and swells.

params.name: Pickup
params.description: Where the pickup sits along the string, from the bridge to the neck. Near the bridge is thin and bright; near the neck is round and flutey.

params.name: Position
params.description: Where the string is picked. Close to the bridge is wiry and nasal; further over the neck is soft and hollow.

params.name: Hardness
params.description: How hard the pick is, from the flesh of a thumb to a stiff plectrum. Harder is brighter with more click at the start of each note.

params.name: Sustain
params.description: How long a held note rings before it has died away. High notes ring for less time than low ones, as they do on a real neck.

params.name: Tone
params.description: The guitar's tone control: where the pickup's resonant peak sits. Lower is dull and woolly; higher is glassy and bright.

params.name: Swell
params.description: Fades each note in, as a volume pedal does, so the pick is hidden and the string seems to bloom. At zero notes start at once.

params.name: Strum
params.description: Spreads the notes of a chord in time from the lowest string to the highest. At zero they sound together; longer is a slow drag across the strings.

params.name: Shimmer
params.description: How fast each string beats against itself as it rings. Low is a slow, living sustain; high gives the chime of a twelve string.

params.name: Warmth
params.description: How hard the amplifier is pushed. Low is clean; higher thickens and compresses the sound until hard notes just begin to break up.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many notes stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. It models a solid-body electric guitar played clean into a valve combo amplifier, after the research brief for this instrument (strings.md, sections 0 and 1): each note is two polarisations of one string (kit::PluckedString, an extended Karplus-Strong loop after Jaffe and Smith, with the loop filter of Valimaki et al.), read through a pickup comb whose fraction of the sounding string follows the fret (Tillman), then a pickup resonance, a soft amplifier stage, a mid scoop and a speaker roll-off. Simplified: one sliding pickup with no two-pickup or humbucker setting, no natural harmonics, no tension modulation, dead spots or vibrato arm, a mono output, and a strum ordered by pitch. The research's sources were found by search and not read, so its figures are from general knowledge. These are choices, not measurements of an instrument: the pickup distances (42 to 162 mm on a 648 mm scale), the inharmonicity of each string, how decay time falls with pitch and frequency, the split and decay ratio of the two polarisations, the resonance height, the scoop, and the speaker's corner frequencies. It is not a circuit model or a sample emulation, and nobody has listened to it: every trait was set by measurement in cpp/test/guitar_test.cpp.
